title: The impact of prophylactic azithromycin on the developing preterm gut microbiome and resistome.
authors: Ahearn-Ford S, Aboklaish A, Young GR, Lowe J, Masi AC, Gallacher D, Marchesi JR, Berrington JE
abstract: Early-life antibiotic exposure can profoundly impact the developing preterm gut microbiome and resistome, with short- and long-term consequences for health. In a large multi-center (n = 28) study of 693 preterm infants, we investigated the effects of 10 d of prophylactic intravenous azithromycin on the gut microbiome and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). The AZithromycin ThErapy for Chronic Lung Disease of Prematurity (AZTEC) study was a double blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of preterm infants (born < 30 weeks of gestation), treated from birth for 10 d with either intravenous azithromycin or placebo, and sampled longitudinally for 21 d or discharge. Using 16S rRNA gene sequencing, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and quantitative PCR, we show azithromycin reduced microbial diversity and the relative abundance of health-associated Bifidobacterium and increased relative abundances of pathobionts Staphylococcus and Enterobacter/Klebsiella. This early azithromycin treatment increased the number of macrolide-resistant genes, including the presence of erm (C), which persisted for the duration of the study. Probiotic use (at individual unit discretion) increased alpha diversity and Bifidobacterium relative abundance, but did not fully mitigate the effects of azithromycin receipt. Combined azithromycin and probiotics further increased the enrichment of Enterobacter/Klebsiella and total ARGs, including erm(C). These findings highlight the impacts of antibiotic and probiotic use, both important in balancing infection control issues and microbiome disruption and antimicrobial resistance.

title: Effects on health and antioxidant status of oral supplementation of hazelnut skin extract in dairy calves with neonatal diarrhea: a randomized clinical trial in hospitalized patients.
authors: Boccardo A, Sannazzaro M, Sala G, Gazzola E, Martucci I, Curone G, Castrica M, Ferrulli V
abstract: Neonatal calf diarrhea (NCD) is a major contributor to morbidity and mortality in calves. Growing concern about antimicrobial resistance has spurred interest in phytotherapeutic alternatives, particularly polyphenol-rich extracts. Hazelnut skin (HS), a by-product of the confectionery sector, is a sustainable and underutilized source of polyphenols; however, its therapeutic efficacy in calves with NCD remains insufficiently investigated. This randomized, parallel-group clinical trial evaluated the effects of oral HS extract supplementation as an adjunct to standard medical therapy in hospitalized dairy calves with NCD. Sixty female Holstein calves were randomly allocated to a control group (CTRL; n = 30) or a treatment group (HS; n = 30) receiving 10 g/day of HS extract with milk for 5 days. All calves received standardized clinical management, including fluid therapy and antimicrobial administration. Clinical parameters, milk intake, body weight, hospitalization outcomes, sepsis scores, and blood oxidative stress biomarkers were monitored. No significant differences were detected between groups for clinical recovery, fecal score, hydration status, milk intake, weight gain, hospitalization duration, mortality, or oxidative stress markers. Clinical improvement over time was evident in both groups and was attributable to standard therapy. In conclusion, short-term oral supplementation with HS extract did not confer additional clinical or antioxidant benefits when added to conventional treatment in calves with NCD.

title: Comorbid asthma - occurrence and associations with patient-related outcomes in COPD: a cohort study.
authors: Athlin Å, Lisspers K, Hasselgren M, Ställberg B, Sandelowsky H, Giezeman M, Janson C, Kisiel MA
journal: Scandinavian journal of primary health care
abstract: PURPOSE: Clinical features of COPD and asthma overlap, complicating differential diagnosis. This study investigated the prevalence of comorbid asthma in COPD patients and its association with patient-related outcomes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients with a doctor's diagnosis of COPD were randomly selected in two cohorts 2005 (n = 1060) and 2014 (n = 1671), from primary and secondary care in Sweden. Data were collected from medical records and patient questionnaires at baseline and at follow-up (2012 and 2022, respectively). Questionnaires included data on exacerbations. Symptoms were assessed using the clinical COPD questionnaire (CCQ). Comorbid asthma was identified through medical records. Ten-year mortality data were obtained from national registers. Logistic and linear regression assessed associations with patient-reported outcomes; Cox regression was applied for mortality analyses. RESULTS: Comorbid asthma was found in 22% of the 2005 cohort and 9% of the 2014 cohort (p < .001). In both cohorts, it was associated with an increased risk of exacerbations: OR (95% CI) 1.58 (1.07-2.32), p = .02, and 2.20 (1.38-3.52), p < .001, respectively. No associations were found between comorbid asthma and worsening of health status (CCQ). Mortality risk did not differ in the 2005 cohort, HR (95% CI) 0.92 (0.71-1.18), but was lower in the 2014 cohort, HR (95% CI) 0.67 (0.49-0.93), p = .02. CONCLUSION: Comorbid asthma in COPD has changed from 22 to 9%, potentially due to improved diagnostics. Comorbid asthma remains clinically relevant due to its association with an increased exacerbation risk.

title: The application progress of detection technology for Bacillus cereus in food: Challenges, innovations and future prospects.
authors: Zhang Y, Zhang X, Zheng H, Wang H, Yu M, Jia W, Jia Z, Cui J
abstract: Food safety is a key issue of global public health. As a foodborne pathogen - Bacillus cereus (B. cereus), it is widely distributed in nature and can cause diseases in both humans and animals. The rapid detection of B. cereus is of great significance for the prevention and control of such diseases. This article provides a detailed overview of the development of B. cereus detection techniques in food, transitioning from traditional methods to a series of current technologies such as immunology, molecular biology and MALDI-TOF-MS. The principles, advantages and disadvantages of various detection techniques, as well as their application progress, were outlined. Furthermore, the application and advantages of combining different techniques in the detection of B. cereus in food were demonstrated. The CRISPR/Cas system possesses the characteristics of high specificity, high sensitivity and ease of operation, and shows great potential in the field of foodborne pathogen detection. This article also explains that the combination of CRISPR/Cas technology with RPA, LFA and AI technologies can further enhance the detection rate and accuracy. The aforementioned technology can enable the early detection and prevention of B. cereus in food, ensuring food safety and preventing the outbreak of foodborne diseases. This article has certain reference value in the research on the detection techniques of B. cereus and other foodborne pathogens in food, and provides strong support for safeguarding food safety and maintaining human health.

title: Integrating high-resolution proximity labelling with orthogonal interactome benchmarks: Insights from Kinetoplastid systems.
authors: Ata A, Topuz Ata D, Odacı ZT
abstract: Proximity labelling has progressed from a specialised protein interaction methodology into a pivotal component of modern spatial proteomics. This review presents a comprehensive overview of the technological development of proximity labelling methodologies for mapping proximal protein associations, encompassing first-generation BioID platforms to advanced systems including TurboID, XL-BioID, APEX2 and UltraID. Special emphasis is placed on advances in labelling kinetics, enzyme miniaturisation, conditional activation, and spatial precision. The convergence of proximity labelling with orthogonal tag-free strategies, such as size-exclusion chromatography-mass spectrometry and cross-linking mass spectrometry, is further examined alongside emerging CRISPR-Cas9-based endogenous tagging and artificial intelligence-driven structural prediction frameworks. These complementary strategies are discussed in the context of their potential contribution to reshaping next-generation interactomics. With kinetoplastids as an illustrative model system, reported proximity labelling investigations in Leishmania, Trypanosoma brucei, and Trypanosoma cruzi are systematically consolidated. Critical challenges include parasite-specific biotin metabolism, oxidative stress linked with peroxidase-based labelling, limitations in endogenous tagging, and the extensive dark proteome impeding functional annotation. Next-generation technologies and artificial intelligence-driven interactomics are further explored within kinetoplastid biology, while emphasising their broader potential to combine high-resolution proximity labelling, orthogonal tag-free benchmarking, genome engineering, and artificial intelligence-driven structural analysis across various biological systems, thereby advancing comprehensive interactome mapping and functional proteome annotation. SIGNIFICANCE: Interactomics is a key pillar of systems biology, offering the indispensable functional framework that transforms protein catalogues into dynamic and predictive models of biological systems. To the best of our knowledge, this review represents one of the most comprehensive syntheses integrating all reported proximity labelling implementations in Leishmania, Trypanosoma brucei, and Trypanosoma cruzi up to 2026. Its importance lies in bringing together the development of proximity labelling into a multi-layered methodological framework that now includes robust reference datasets, such as the recently reported large-scale physical interactomes of L. donovani (16,095 interactions) and T. cruzi, generated employing SEC-MS and XL-MS methodologies. Through addressing the "dark proteome," this review positions proximity labelling within a broader multi-modal interactomics framework integrating SEC-MS, XL-MS, and AI-assisted structural modelling, while offering a structured roadmap built around next-generation technologies, including PerTurboID for perturbations, iAPEX for redox challenges, and CRISPR-Cas for physiological tagging. Collectively, these advances may facilitate the development of increasingly predictive and spatially resolved interactome models across complex biological systems.

title: Machine learning algorithms empower traditional Chinese medicine: Breakthrough approaches from chemical component analysis to pharmacological mechanism research.
authors: Han Z, Zhao F, Xu H, Zhang Z, Wu J, Zhang Y, Pan J, Li M
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine studies are constrained by complex chemical components and multi-target biological interactions, making conventional analytical methods inefficient for mechanism exploration. As a data-driven technique, machine learning has been widely adopted to tackle diverse complex challenges in TCM research. Nevertheless, most existing reviews merely summarize individual algorithms or scattered application cases, lacking systematic task-based classification and unified operational standards. Based on literature published from 2022 to 2026, this review systematically classifies machine learning applications in TCM into four core research tasks. A task-oriented framework is constructed to match different algorithms with appropriate TCM research scenarios. This paper further establishes a complete standardized workflow covering algorithm selection, model construction and model evaluation to standardize ML applications in TCM research. This review also summarizes the applications of machine learning in TCM quality control, bioactive compound identification, processing analysis, and mechanism elucidation. Furthermore, major bottlenecks in current ML-based TCM studies are analyzed, and feasible optimization strategies are proposed. This review aims to provide clear and practical guidelines for the standardized application of machine learning in future TCM research.

title: Analysis of multidimensional molecular mechanisms in Parkinson's disease and precise therapeutic strategies.
authors: Chen X, Zhao Z, Shen Y, Ji Y, Yao X, Gu X, Qi L, Sun H
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD), the second most common neurodegenerative disorder worldwide, is characterized by progressive loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra and striatal dopamine deficiency, leading to motor dysfunction. The complex pathogenesis involves impaired protein homeostasis with α-synuclein aggregation, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and neuroinflammation, including NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Newly identified regulated cell death pathways - including ferroptosis, cuproptosis, pyroptosis, and necroptosis - have further expanded current understanding of PD pathology, while gut-brain axis interactions may contribute to peripheral-central communication and disease progression. These mechanistic insights inspire targeted therapeutic strategies comprising α-synuclein inhibitors, mitochondrial protectants, anti-inflammatory agents, and novel cell death pathway blockers, alongside gut-brain axis interventions. However, these approaches face substantial challenges including limited blood-brain barrier penetration, insufficient target specificity, and individual genetic heterogeneity. Future research should prioritize developing multi-target combination therapies, integrating multi-omics and computational approaches for biomarker identification and patient stratification, while advancing clinical translation of gene- and cell-based therapies. Through interdisciplinary collaboration and precision medicine implementation, disease-modifying treatments for PD may become increasingly feasible.

title: Understanding genetic determinants of bacterial adaptation to plant niches: Toward more robust bioinoculant design.
authors: Villa-Rodríguez E, Ferguson S, Stougaard J, Radutoiu S
abstract: Plant-associated bacteria offer a sustainable alternative to chemical inputs in agriculture, yet the field performance of microbial inoculants remains inconsistent. A central but frequently overlooked cause is that bioprospecting pipelines still select strains on the basis of plant-growth-promoting activities, while the bacterial genetic traits that determine whether a strain can reach, colonise and persist in a given root compartment are rarely assessed. Previous reviews have largely catalogued growth-promoting functions or described root microbiome assembly from the plant's perspective, here we take the bacterium's. We trace the journey of a bacterium from bulk soil to its final niche and, at each stage, identify the genes and pathways (genetic determinants) that encode key bacterial traits involved, such as chemotaxis and motility, nutrient acquisition and metabolic independence, competitive and defensive arsenals, attachment and biofilm formation, evasion of plant immunity, and endophytic entry and persistence. Throughout, we use evidence from comparative genomics and metagenomics, (meta)transcriptomics, targeted mutagenesis and genome-wide screens such as Tn-seq, obtained in systems ranging from binary interactions to synthetic communities and natural soils. For each stage we examine the current state of knowledge, identify critical gaps, and propose avenues to deepen our mechanistic understanding of the bacterial traits involved in plant colonisation. We argue that this mechanistic understanding is the missing foundation for developing inoculants with more consistent and robust performance across diverse agroecosystems.

title: Programmable histone acetylation enables reversible regulation of cellulase production in Myceliophthora thermophila.
authors: Li Y, Zhao X, Yang X, Wang J, Liu D, Yu Q, Liu Q, Tian C
abstract: Myceliophthora thermophila is a thermophilic filamentous fungus with great potential for biomass biorefining and industrial protein production. However, the locus-specific epigenetic regulation of the cellulolytic network in this fungus remains poorly understood. Here, we established a CRISPR/dCas9-p300 system that recruits the p300 histone acetyltransferase to target loci and targeted the promoters of the key cellulolytic regulators clr-1, clr-2, and xyr-1. Targeted recruitment of dCas9-p300 increased the transcription of these regulators by up to 5.2-fold and promoter-associated histone acetylation by approximately 2- to 3-fold. Simultaneous targeting of all three regulators resulted in greater increases than single-locus targeting, with extracellular protein production and CMCase activity increasing by up to 5.5- and 3.7-fold, respectively. The dependence of these effects on guide RNA-directed targeting and p300 catalytic activity was confirmed using no-guide controls and the p300 inhibitor A-485. A catalytically inactive p300 mutant targeting clr-2 failed to enhance clr-2 transcription, extracellular protein production, or CMCase activity. We further developed an inducible dCas9-p300 system to examine the persistence and reversibility of the activated state. Following inducer withdrawal, the high cellulase-production phenotype was maintained during the initial propagation but gradually declined over successive passages and was restored upon re-induction. These results demonstrate that targeted histone acetylation can coordinately activate an endogenous cellulolytic regulatory network and establish a reversible high-production state without altering the DNA sequences of the target loci. This work provides a chromatin-based strategy for reversible regulation of endogenous gene networks and protein production in filamentous fungi.

title: Zygote origin shapes sensitivity to electrical voltage field and editing susceptibility after CRISPR/Cas9-RNP electroporation in bovine embryos.
authors: Rahimi M, Miskel D, Schreiber M, Habermann H, Haake L, Brenig B, Besenfelder U, Havlicek V
abstract: Despite major progress in generation of edited embryos and offspring via CRISPR/Cas9-RNP electroporation, editing outcomes remain highly variable. This variability may be due to intrinsic differences between in vivo-derived (IVV) and in vitro-derived (IVT) zygotes, which may play a more decisive role than previously anticipated. Therefore, this study aimed to determine how zygote origin shapes the sensitivity to electrical voltage field and editing susceptibility after CRISPR/Cas9-RNP electroporation in the bovine model. The present study systematically compared subsequent developmental competence and editing events in IVV- and IVT-derived bovine zygotes across defined electroporation voltages and pulse durations. Notably, CRISPR/Cas9-RNP electroporation of IVV-derived bovine zygotes of comparable age and collected by tubal embryo flushing (10-18 h post ovulation, hpo) resulted in markedly lower survival rates at 25 and 30 V compared to 20 V. In contrast, higher (p < 0.05) editing frequencies were observed at 25 V and 30 V. Clear differences, however, were observed between the two zygote groups. Following CRISPR/Cas9 RNP electroporation, IVV-derived zygotes yielded a higher proportion of unedited blastocysts (p < 0.05), absence of full edited embryos, a significantly increased frequency of monoallelic edits and reduced rates of mosaicism compared to IVT-derived zygotes. Collectively, the results of the present study clearly underscore a significant lower editing efficiency to pulse sensitivity ratio in IVV-derived zygotes compared to their IVT counterparts. To our knowledge, this is the first study to use bovine IVV-derived zygotes for genome editing using RNP-electroporation to elucidate how zygote origin shapes sensitivity to electrical voltage field and editing efficiency.

title: Aptamer-functionalized EGCG nanocarrier for neutrophil-targeted AKBA delivery promotes anxiety-related fracture healing.
authors: Ouyang L, Zhang Y, Liao J, Zhang Z, He X, Lin Z, Tao R, Xie X
abstract: Anxiety is clinically associated with impaired fracture healing, but the underlying immunological mechanism remains unclear, and no targeted therapy is available. In a mouse model of chronic restraint stress (CRS)-induced anxiety with femoral fracture, we observed expansion of TGFβ1+CCR5+ double-positive neutrophils in the bone marrow. These neutrophils inhibited osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) via TGFβ1 secretion, while BMSC-derived CCL5 reciprocally promoted neutrophil activation, forming a detrimental feedback that disrupted fracture repair. Mechanistically, CRS activated the NF-κB-CCR5 axis to upregulate CCR5 and sustain this neutrophil subset. We found that acetyl-11-keto-β-boswellic acid (AKBA) directly bound YAP1, relieved YAP1-mediated suppression of ubiquitin-specific peptidase 31 (USP31), and consequently inhibited NF-κB phosphorylation and CCR5 expression, reducing the pathogenic neutrophil population and restoring BMSCs' osteogenic function. In order to overcome the problems of poor solubility, low bioavailability and tissue non-selectivity of AKBA, we developed a NIMP-R14 aptamer-modified epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG)-coated nanocarrier (AKBA@E-N), which can achieve enhanced uptake and local retention of neutrophils in the acidic microenvironment of the fracture site. In vivo, AKBA@E-N significantly accelerated fracture healing compared with free AKBA. This study reveals a neutrophil-mediated mechanism linking stress to impaired bone repair and provides a targeted nanotherapeutic strategy.

title: Tissue engineering polymeric formulations enable lymphangiogenesis for myocardial repair.
authors: Liu Z, Li R, Huang W, Zhang J, Qu Y, Dong W, Liu Y, Li Q
abstract: PURPOSE: Emerging evidence emphasizes the pivotal contribution of cardiac lymphatic activation following ischemic heart injury, with induced lymphangiogenesis driving edema resolution and inflammatory cell clearance. The aim of this study was to identify a bioactive small molecule with pro-lymphangiogenic activity and to develop a tissue engineering polymeric formulation for sustained local delivery in myocardial repair. METHODS: Through a high-throughput screen, we identified the bioactive molecule β-(3,4-dihydroxyphenyl) lactic acid (3,4-DHPLA) as a potent stimulator of lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs). To leverage this finding, we engineered a tissue engineering polymeric formulation (TEPF) to promote lymphangiogenesis during myocardial repair. The TEPF was fabricated via an integrated strategy combining 3D printing and near-field electrospinning to incorporate 3,4-DHPLA into a biodegradable polyurethane scaffold. The resulting structure mimics the microstructure of the cardiac extracellular matrix while supporting the microenvironment-responsive release of 3,4-DHPLA. RESULTS: We evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of TEPF in rat and porcine ischemia/reperfusion injury models, which markedly improved cardiac function and significantly attenuated adverse ventricular remodeling. Single-cell RNA sequencing and in vitro data further revealed the dual mechanisms of TEPF, not only promoting lymphangiogenesis but also orchestrating a pro-regenerative niche via expansion of Tregs, M2 macrophages, and pro-regenerative fibroblasts (COL12A1+, COL11A1+, NRG1+). CONCLUSIONS: Thus, the tissue engineering polymeric formulations may enable sustained drug release during myocardial tissue repair, thereby alleviating the pain of injection administration for patients with cardiovascular diseases and potentially facilitating patient-friendly use of other functional molecules-based therapeutic tissue engineering formulations through durable delivery.

title: DiFVM: A Vectorized Graph-Based Finite Volume Solver for Differentiable CFD on Unstructured Meshes.
authors: Du P, Li Y, Xu M, Wang JX
abstract: Differentiable programming has emerged as an important tool for gradient-based inverse problems and end-to-end hybrid physics-machine learning in computational fluid dynamics. Existing differentiable CFD platforms predominantly rely on structured Cartesian grids, limiting their direct application to geometrically complex domains where body-conforming unstructured discretizations are essential. We present DiFVM, the first GPU-native, end-to-end differentiable finite-volume (FV) CFD solver for incompressible flow on unstructured polyhedral meshes. The central methodological contribution is a graph-based computational reformulation of the complete unstructured FV/PISO solution procedure: by expressing FV operators as static scatter/gather primitives on the mesh connectivity graph, DiFVM transforms irregular unstructured connectivity into a GPU-compatible computational representation. All operations are implemented in JAX/XLA, providing just-in-time compilation, operator fusion, and automatic differentiation through the complete simulation pipeline. Differentiable Windkessel outlet boundary conditions are provided for cardiovascular applications, and DiFVM accepts standard OpenFOAM case directories without modification for seamless adoption in existing workflows. Forward accuracy is assessed through analytical and canonical benchmark problems, comparisons with published reference data, and independent solver comparisons, while end-to-end differentiability is demonstrated through proof-of-concept inverse modeling examples. DiFVM provides a differentiable CFD framework for gradient-based optimization, inverse modeling and future physics-integrated machine learning on complex unstructured geometries.

title: The ups and downs of human UNC93B1: Autoimmune and viral conditions.
authors: Idiiatullina E, Casanova JL, Zhang SY
abstract: Mouse Unc93b1 was identified in 2006 by forward genetics as an ER membrane protein essential for the activity of the endosomal nucleic acid-sensing receptors TLR3, TLR7, and TLR9. In vitro studies in mouse and human cells have revealed its cellular functions, including ER-based stabilization and trafficking of endosomal TLR proteins (TLR3, TLR7, TLR8, and TLR9) and regulation of signaling thresholds through competitive trafficking control (TLR7 and TLR9). Human genetic studies have clarified the physiological role of UNC93B1 in natural conditions. Biallelic loss-of-function UNC93B1 mutations impair TLR3 signaling in central nervous system-resident cells, thereby conferring a predisposition to HSV-1 encephalitis. UNC93B1 deficiency may also predispose to other viral infections, as suggested by patients with inherited TLR3 or TLR7 deficiency. Conversely, monoallelic or biallelic UNC93B1 gain-of-function variants enhancing TLR7 and/or TLR8 signaling predispose patients to autoimmunity and inflammation, including early-onset systemic lupus erythematosus and chilblain lupus. Thus, in humans, UNC93B1 maintains a delicate balance between host defense and tolerance to self.

title: Reprogramming NOX4-associated ferro-aging with an iron-chelating senescent-cell-targeted therapy for intervertebral disc degeneration.
authors: Wang J, Chen Q, Xing J, Sun Y, Yan C, Zhao B, Han L, Sun J
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) has been a major contributor to chronic low back pain, yet effective disease-modifying therapies remain limited. Here, we identified a NOX4-associated ferro-aging program linking iron overload, oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation, and cellular senescence in degenerative NPCs. Clinical imaging, transcriptomic analyses, human disc specimens, iron-overloaded NPCs, and naturally aged rats consistently revealed ferro-aging-associated changes during IVDD. Mechanistically, gain- and loss-of-function, genetic rescue, and temporal analyses positioned NOX4 as an upstream oxidative regulator of ROS-dependent ACSL4 activation, lipid peroxidation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and NPC senescence. Natural-product screening identified amentoflavone (Amen) as a candidate NOX4-interacting compound that suppresses membrane-associated NADPH oxidase activity in a NOX4-dependent manner. Single-cell transcriptomic analyses showed that ferro-aging NPCs exhibited increased NKG2D ligand-related stress signals, reduced endocytic activity, and enhanced membrane-fusion features. Guided by these characteristics, we engineered SenoFAN, an Amen-loaded, iron-chelating phenolic nanozyme coated with NKG2D-engineered NPC membranes. SenoFAN integrates iron sequestration, nanozyme-mediated redox remodeling, Amen-mediated NOX4-dependent suppression of NADPH oxidase activity, and ferro-aging-cell-adapted delivery through NKG2D-ligand recognition and membrane fusion. In vitro, SenoFAN reduced labile iron and oxidative stress, restored mitochondrial and lipid homeostasis, and suppressed lipid peroxidation and senescence. In a rat puncture-induced IVDD model, SenoFAN showed preferential association with ferro-aging-associated NPCs, prolonged intradiscal retention, reduced iron deposition and senescence, preserved disc structure, and showed favorable biosafety. Collectively, our findings identify NOX4-associated ferro-aging as a therapeutically actionable pathological program in IVDD, while establishing an upstream regulatory role for NOX4 in the FAC-induced ferro-aging model.

title: Discovery and characterization of potent and efficacious small-molecule parathyroid hormone Receptor-1 (PTH1R) antagonists for the treatment of hypercalcemia.
authors: Pontillo J, Wang S, Zhu Y, Rico-Bautista E, Shintaku J, Urgaonkar S, Antwan A, Betz SF
abstract: Primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) is caused by the enlargement and overactivation of one or more of the parathyroid glands, via parathyroid adenomas or hyperplasia. This results in over-secretion of PTH hormone, which results in agonism of PTH1R and subsequent hypercalcemia. Blocking PTH action via an oral, small-molecule PTH1R antagonist may provide a convenient and improved therapy for PHPT. Herein, we report the discovery, optimization and characterization of a highly potent, bioavailable and efficacious series represented by 9c (hPTH1R IC50 = 5.2 nM), which based on pharmacokinetics and biological activity, represents a significant preclinical advancement in the development of small-molecule PTH antagonists.

title: Integrated SEM, TEM and CLSM workflow for tegumental analysis of adult Schistosoma mansoni.
authors: de Carvalho Augusto R, João RCF, Barbosa HS, Mello-Silva CC, Santos CP
abstract: The tegument of Schistosoma mansoni is a key host-parasite interface and a major target for drug and vaccine development. Although ultrastructural studies of the tegument date back decades, methodological inconsistencies often complicate comparisons across studies. Here, we present a standardized, easy-to-use framework for investigating tegumental architecture using three complementary techniques: scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM). We provide step-by-step protocols, highlight strengths and limitations of each method, and illustrate their outputs using adult male worms. We also outline a scheme for unbiased quantitative analysis of the resulting images and indicate how the protocols can be adapted to female worms, to other developmental stages and schistosome species, and to immunolocalization at the ultrastructural level. This integrative pipeline enables reproducible morphological characterization and facilitates downstream applications in pharmacology, immunology, and parasite biology.

Sensitive detection of 4-hydroxy-2-nonenal-modified proteins in oxidative stress-related diseases.
authors: Méndez-Cuadro D, Kamali AN, Ruiz C, Pérez-Benavente S, Hernáez ML, Rodríguez-Cavallo E, Puyet A, Bautista JM
abstract: Protein modification by 4-hydroxy-2-nonenal (HNE) is associated with metabolic, neurodegenerative, and infectious diseases characterized by oxidative stress. Detecting low-abundance HNE-protein adducts in complex extracts requires antibodies with suitable reactivity and selectivity. We generated polyclonal antisera in rabbits using matched-species rabbit serum albumin modified in vitro with HNE (RSA-HNE), administered either intact or after tryptic digestion. The antisera displayed distinct recognition profiles across dot blot, ELISA, and Western blot assays using HNE-modified standards and membrane-protein extracts from uninfected and Plasmodium falciparum-infected human erythrocytes. Antiserum 1, raised against intact RSA-HNE, showed the stronger overall immunochemical response, whereas Antiserum 2, raised against tryptic RSA-HNE, displayed a different and more restricted peptide-recognition profile. In an immunoenrichment and LC-MS/MS workflow, Antiserum 1 recovered 14 candidate HNE-associated membrane proteins from erythrocytes infected with P. falciparum trophozoites. Site-specific evidence remained tentative for four peptides. These antisera are therefore proposed as research tools for studying protein lipoxidation, although biological replication and orthogonal validation of the candidate modification sites are required.

title: CATH-1 supplementation improves sperm quality and fertility of rooster semen during cold storage by reducing bacterial contamination.
authors: Authaida S, Boonkum W, Duangjinda M, Shimada M, Kaeoket K, Rerkyusuke S, Chankitisakul V
abstract: The present study investigated the effects of antibiotic and antimicrobial peptide supplementation on semen quality, viable bacterial load, and fertility potential in Thai native chickens during cold storage. Semen samples were diluted in an extender supplemented with kanamycin (31.20 μg/mL) or CATH-1 (3.75 or 7.50 μg/mL) and stored at 5 °C for up to 72 h. Sperm quality parameters, viable bacterial load, and reproductive outcomes following artificial insemination were assessed at 0, 24, 48, and 72 h. Storage duration significantly affected all sperm quality parameters (P < 0.001), while fertility and hatchability were progressively lower across the sequential storage-time phases. Kanamycin and CATH-1 at 3.75 μg/mL consistently maintained higher sperm quality and reduced susceptibility to lipid peroxidation compared with the control (P < 0.05), with no significant difference between the two treatments. Both treatments effectively suppressed bacterial proliferation; however, viable bacterial load increased progressively beyond 24 h in all groups. Scanning electron microscopy revealed marked bacterial surface alterations following CATH-1 treatment, consistent with membrane-disruptive antibacterial activity. In contrast, CATH-1 at 7.50 μg/mL compromised sperm quality and reproductive outcomes from the initial time point onward, despite achieving the greatest bacterial suppression among all treatments. Across the sequential storage-time phases, fertility potential was progressively lower, although the kanamycin and CATH-1 (3.75 μg/mL) groups maintained higher fertility than the control during prolonged storage. These findings demonstrate a dose-dependent dual effect of CATH-1, with 3.75 μg/mL performing comparably to kanamycin and representing a promising antibiotic alternative in the context of One Health concerns in poultry artificial insemination programs.

title: Implementing a First Nation data-sovereign and agile modelling platform for pandemic management: lessons from Manitoba.
authors: Phillips-Beck W, Lavoie JG, Star L, Nickel N, Romanescu R
abstract: This paper describes lessons learned from a partnership between the First Nations Health and Social Secretariat of Manitoba (FNHSSM) and researchers at the University of Manitoba to develop a community-led COVID-19 modelling platform. The envisioned tool would allow First Nations leaders to input local data and generate outputs to support decision-making using a stochastic, age-stratified agent-based model of COVID-19 transmission. Although the platform was not fully operationalized during the project, several important lessons emerged. First, the COVID-19 pandemic placed significant demands on human resources, making such an ambitious initiative difficult to implement during an active public health emergency. Second, the project required coordination among multiple teams with distinct expertise, including model developers, dashboard designers, and FNHSSM information technology staff responsible for infrastructure planning. Competing pandemic-related priorities frequently delayed collaboration and implementation. Third, access to administrative data through the Manitoba Centre for Health Policy involved a six-month reporting lag, limiting the availability of timely information needed for emergency response and decision-making. These challenges highlight structural barriers to data-driven pandemic management in First Nations communities. We recommend: (1) providing First Nations organizations and communities with ongoing access to their own administrative data for service delivery, planning, and emergency management; and (2) establishing First Nations-led data centres with sustainable infrastructure and core funding to support data sovereignty, agile reporting, and future public health response efforts.

title: Balancing individual risks and collective benefits: Effects of vaccine price, message framing, and value orientations on influenza vaccination in China.
authors: Chu Y, Jiang Y, Cheng Q, Zha X, Wang Y, Liang W, Chen L
abstract: Vaccines are widely recognized as effective tools for preventing infectious diseases; however, vaccine hesitancy remains a persistent global challenge that undermines herd immunity and public health efforts. This study investigates how message framing and value orientation impact Chinese university students' willingness to receive the influenza vaccination at different price points, aiming to inform strategies for promoting health behaviors. A 2 (framing: gain, loss) ×2 (value orientation: individualism, collectivism) experimental design was employed with 1,408 Chinese university students to examine influences on vaccination intention. Vaccination intention decreased significantly as vaccine price increased. Compared with the control group, persuasive messages generally increased vaccination intention, and this effect became more pronounced in paid scenarios. When the vaccine was free, differences among message types were not significant. In paid scenarios, loss-framed messages were more persuasive than gain-framed messages, and individualistic-oriented messages were more effective than collectivistic-oriented messages. Among the four message combinations, the individualistic-loss message showed the strongest persuasive effect. Mediation analyses further indicated that perceived severity of influenza and perceived vaccine effectiveness mediated the effect of the individualistic-loss message on vaccination intention. Vaccination intention is influenced by the interaction between vaccine price and message attributes. Free vaccination reduces the relative impact of message variations, whereas paid scenarios provide more room for persuasive messages to operate. In price-sensitive contexts, individualistic-loss messages that emphasize personal infection risks and vaccine effectiveness may be particularly useful for promoting influenza vaccination.

title: Proceedings of the 3rd edition of the International e-Health Forum 2024.
Beyond stroke: atrial fibrillation and the broader burden of thromboembolic events in the population-based EpiHealth study.
authors: Höiby P, Zarrouk M, Lind L, Basna R, Overton MC, Elmståhl S
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the distribution and risk of thromboembolic events (TEs) among adults with and without atrial fibrillation (AF), and to assess oral anticoagulant (OAC) use over time. DESIGN: This population-based longitudinal cohort study included EpiHealth participants recruited between April 2011 and December 2016 and followed through linkage to Swedish health data registers from baseline until the first TE, death, or December 31, 2016. RESULTS: At baseline, 873 of 22,616 participants (3.9%) had AF and 297 developed incident AF during follow-up. 484 participants experienced at least one TE during 70,587 person-years. Participants with AF had higher TE incidence (68 events, 5.9%; p < 0.001), predominantly arterial (73.5%), with 94% of arterial events involving the cerebral circulation. Approximately one quarter of TEs among participants with AF occurred outside the cerebral circulation and comprised both venous and non-cerebral arterial events. Although participants with incident AF represented less than one quarter of participants with AF, they accounted for 40% of TEs in the AF group. OAC use increased from 39.0% to 50.4%, with a shift from predominantly warfarin to direct oral anticoagulants. In time-dependent Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, and prior arterial thromboembolism, untreated AF was associated with increased thromboembolic risk compared with no AF (HR 2.53), whereas OAC use was associated with lower risk. CONCLUSIONS: AF was associated with substantially increased thromboembolic risk, predominantly arterial in nature. One in five TEs among participants with AF coincided with newly diagnosed AF, suggesting potential opportunities for earlier AF detection and timely initiation of anticoagulant treatment.

title: Circulatory arrest versus aortic cross-clamping in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm repair.
authors: Braatz E, Stenman M, Al-Mousli J, Dalén M, Olsson C
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aortic cross‑clamping and mild hypothermic circulatory arrest (MHCA) are commonly used strategies in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm surgery. This study compared these approaches in elective procedures for patients with a distal ascending aortic diameter of 40-50 mm. The primary outcome was a composite of 30‑day mortality, stroke, or acute kidney injury, with secondary outcomes including long‑term survival and postoperative complications. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This single‑center observational cohort included patients treated between 2016 and 2024. Distal ascending aortic diameters were assessed on preoperative computed tomography, and clinical data were obtained from SWEDEHEART. Patients were assigned to aortic cross‑clamp (n = 261) or MHCA (n = 138). Propensity score matching was performed in a 1:1 ratio to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: The composite primary outcome occurred in 15 patients (3.8%) and was more common with MHCA than with cross‑clamp (6.5% vs 2.3%, p = 0.035). Two patients (0.5%), both in the MHCA group, died within 30 days. After matching, the odds ratio for the composite endpoint was 2.4 (95% CI, 0.66-11.5), indicating no significant difference. Long‑term survival was similar between groups (log‑rank p = 0.33). CONCLUSIONS: Both strategies were associated with low perioperative risk and comparable long‑term survival. These results support flexible operative planning, allowing the distal anastomotic technique to be chosen based on individual anatomy and surgical preference.

title: Biomimetic sequential targeted nanoplatform for synergistic thrombolysis in ischemic stroke.
authors: Wang J, Wang X, Liu S, Zheng Y, Wang C, Cheng J, Wang X
abstract: Conventional thrombolytic drugs for vascular blockage such as tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) are challenged by the low bioavailability, off-target side effects and limited penetration in thrombi, leading to delayed recanalization. Herein, we developed a sequential targeted nanoplatform for efficient thrombolysis based on the thrombolysis-neuroprotection integrated strategy. The mesoporous silica layer-modified upconversion nanoparticle (UCNP) was loaded with the nitric oxide (NO) donors (BNN6), further coating platelet membranes (PMs) on the surface of UCNP. tPA was conjugated onto PMs using the MMP9-responsive peptide as a linker to form a multifunctional drug carrier of UCNP/BNN6@PM-tPA. The proposed drug carrier maintained stability in the blood circulation to reduce bleeding risk (protection), facilitating it colonizing at the thrombus clots. MMP-9 triggered the release of tPA to realize rapid thrombolysis (attack), whereas continuous NO release from NIR-irradiated BNN6 acted to prevent vascular re-embolization (defense). In vitro and in vivo evaluation revealed that UCNP/BNN6@PM-tPA enables thrombus-homing accumulation, fluorescence imaging-guided thrombolysis, and NO mediated prevention of thrombosis recurrence, displaying favorable therapeutic outcomes with low bleeding risk. This study offers a facile, safe, and effective way towards the clinical treatment of thrombosis and ischemic stroke.

title: YBX3 promotes ischemia-reperfusion injury by enhancing microglial glycolysis via PKM2 stabilization and mTOR-HIF-1α pathway activation.
authors: Feng Z, Qin P, Ni H, Cao X, Xu J, Yuan Y
abstract: Stroke remains one of the leading causes of death and long-term disability worldwide, with neuroinflammation and metabolic dysfunction playing central roles in its pathogenesis. In this study, we investigated the function of Y-box binding protein 3 (YBX3) in ischemic stroke, with particular focus on its regulation of glycolysis and neuroinflammatory responses. Using a middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model in C57BL/6 mice and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R) model in BV2 microglia, we observed that YBX3 expression was markedly upregulated following ischemia-reperfusion. Overexpression of YBX3 aggravated cerebral infarct size, worsened motor and neurological outcomes, and increased the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β) both in vivo and in vitro. Mechanistically, YBX3 enhanced glycolysis in BV2 cells by stabilizing pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2) mRNA and promoting its expression, while simultaneously activating glycolysis through the mTOR-HIF-1α signaling pathway. Pharmacological inhibition of mTOR with rapamycin reversed YBX3-induced glycolytic activation, neuroinflammation, and neuronal injury. Collectively, these results identify YBX3 as a key regulator of ischemic brain damage through glycolysis-dependent mechanisms and underscore its potential as a therapeutic target for stroke.

title: Guanidine-quaternary ammonium polymer-derived carbon dots differentially modulate bacterial respiration and osteoblast mitochondria to resolve infection and foster osteointegration.
authors: Bai X, Qin A, Wang Z, Kong G, Zhang M, Li H, Zhao R, Yu Y
abstract: Implant-associated infections (IAIs) represent one of the most challenging complications following orthopedic implantation. Current antibacterial strategies struggle to achieve complete pathogen eradication while maintaining sustained osteogenic activity at the implant-bone interface. Leveraging the spatial divergence in energy metabolism between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, we designed and synthesized guanidine-quaternary ammonium polymer-derived carbon dots (GQCDs) with confirmed structure. Under non-infected conditions, GQCDs enhance mitochondrial metabolism to promote bone regeneration. In infected microenvironments, GQCDs not only selectively target bacterial membranes and inhibit the respiratory chain to exert potent antibacterial effects, but also downregulate host inflammatory responses and restore mitochondrial function in osteoblasts, thereby creating a favorable microenvironment for bone repair. GQCDs can be stably integrated onto various clinical implant substrates via a coating process. GQCDs-coated implants possessed the dual antibacterial and osteogenic functionalities, which were validated using in vitro co-culture systems and in vivo implant infection models in rats and beagles, offering a promising strategy with encouraging translational prospects to address IAIs.

title: Investigation of the effect of simulated gastrointestinal digestive fluids on the infectivity of influenza A virus H1N1.
authors: Blondin-Brosseau M, Harlow J, Nasheri N
abstract: The recent emergence of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) in dairy cattle has raised concerns about potential non-respiratory exposure routes including ingestion of contaminated raw milk. In this study, we assessed the survival of influenza A virus (IAV) in milk during simulated human digestion and estimated infection risk using quantitative microbial risk assessment (QMRA). Whole milk artificially inoculated with IAV A(H1N1) was exposed to human saliva, fed-state simulated gastric fluids (pH 3-6) containing pepsin, and fed-state simulated intestinal fluids containing pancreatin, in the presence or absence of mucin. Viral infectivity was quantified using plaque assays. Exposure to saliva did not reduce viral infectivity, whereas gastric inactivation was strongly pH-dependent, ranging from approximately 1 log reduction at pH 6 to about 6 log reduction at pH 3. Complete viral inactivation (>6 log10) was observed following exposure to fed-state intestinal fluid, regardless of mucin presence. Mucin conferred partial protection against gastric inactivation at pH 3 and 4.5. QMRA incorporating experimentally derived inactivation data estimated median probabilities of infection per serving ranging from 1.35 × 10-5 to 1.35 × 10-8 under four dose-response assumptions. Overall, these results indicate that human digestion substantially reduces the infectivity of influenza viruses in contaminated milk and provide quantitative evidence to inform food safety risk assessments for influenza viruses and other enveloped viruses potentially transmitted through raw dairy products.

title: Open-label extension study of leniolisib in activated PI3Kδ syndrome: Long-term efficacy and safety.
authors: Rao VK, Šedivá A, Dalm VASH, Plebani A, Schuetz C, Shcherbina A, Trizzino A, Zharankova Y
abstract: Activated phosphoinositide 3-kinase delta syndrome (APDS) is an inborn error of immunity characterized by immune deficiency and dysregulation. Leniolisib is a selective phosphoinositide 3-kinase delta inhibitor approved to treat APDS in patients ≥12 years old. We report final results from a single-arm, open-label extension study in 37 patients with APDS (NCT02859727). Median leniolisib exposure was 4.3 years (range, 1.2-7.0 years). Adverse events (AE) were reported in 34 patients; 87% were grade 1. Serious AEs, reported in 10 patients, were deemed unrelated to leniolisib. Two patients discontinued treatment due to AEs: cardiac arrest and Hodgkin's lymphoma. There were significant reductions in annual infection (P = 0.0005) and respiratory infection (P = 0.0017) rates per year of treatment. Immunoglobulin replacement therapy (IRT) use significantly decreased per year of treatment (P = 0.0095). Clinically meaningful improvements in general health scores from the 36-Item Short Form Survey were observed. Overall, long-term use of leniolisib was generally well tolerated, and infections and IRT use reduced over time.

title: Nutrient availability and sodium pyruvate regulate the resuscitation of viable but nonculturable Staphylococcus aureus.
authors: Yu H, Ge R, Du J, Hua Y, Zhao F
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) can enter a viable but nonculturable (VBNC) state when induced by citric acid at 4 °C, posing hidden risks to food safety upon resuscitation. However, the effects of nutritional conditions and sodium pyruvate (SP) on this process remain unclear. This study demonstrates that 0.5 × TSB, TSB, 2 × TSB, and SP resuscitate VBNC cells following sigmoidal kinetics, with an efficacy ranking of SP > 2 × TSB > TSB > 0.5 × TSB. SP significantly accelerated resuscitation through enhanced early enzymatic activity, a transient increase in intracellular ROS levels, and rapid ATP accumulation, accompanied by dynamic nucleic acid fluctuations peaking at 10-12 h. Furthermore, proteomic profiling and targeted inhibition analyses revealed that DNA repair and cell wall biosynthesis are critically involved in initiating resuscitation, whereas signal transduction and respiratory metabolism primarily govern post-resuscitation growth. Practically, a 5-h or 10-h pre-resuscitation in 2 × TSB successfully detected VBNC S. aureus in high pressure processing-treated apple juice during 4 °C storage, which was undetectable via direct enumeration. These findings offer mechanistic insights into pathogen resuscitation and provide practical strategies for food safety risk assessment and detection.
